title: Four Friends Turned a Thailand Street Snack Into a Rs 50 Crore Brand
excerpt: The Croffle Guys landed ₹2.5 crore from Kunal Bahl and Mohit Yadav on Shark Tank India — a ₹50 crore valuation built on croissant-dough waffles and zero ad spend.
body:
• The Croffle Guys — founded by Annanya Agarwal, Veer Pinto, Amay Thakkar and Rahul Vohra — was valued at ₹50 crore after raising ₹2.5 crore for 5% equity from Kunal Bahl and Mohit Yadav on the Shark Tank India Season 5 premiere (January 2026).
  • The idea came from a 2025 Thailand trip, where the friends watched a street vendor press croissant dough in a waffle iron — a "croffle": flaky croissant layers with a crisp waffle texture.
  • A key caveat: the ₹50-crore figure is a valuation, not revenue. First-year lifetime sales were about ₹1.5 crore, with ~70% gross margins and store-level EBITDA positive.
  • The brand opened its first Mumbai outlet deliberately opposite a Belgian Waffle Co. to prove product-market fit, and has since launched in Delhi.

Four Mumbai friends discovered a street snack in Thailand, pressed it into a waffle iron, and turned it into a brand that investors valued at ₹50 crore. The Croffle Guys, founded by Annanya Agarwal, Veer Pinto, Amay Thakkar and Rahul Vohra, landed ₹2.5 crore for 5% equity from Kunal Bahl and Mohit Yadav on the Shark Tank India Season 5 premiere in January 2026 — a round reported as a rare all-shark bidding war, with all five sharks competing.

The Thailand discovery

A croffle is exactly what it sounds like: croissant dough pressed in a waffle iron, producing flaky croissant layers with a crisp, caramelized waffle texture. The four friends encountered it at a Thai street vendor's cart in 2025. Rahul Vohra, who comes from the film industry and has worked with filmmaker Kabir Khan, gave the brand its visual and content voice; the group bet on a single-product QSR model — croffles plus beverages — with zero performance marketing, growing instead on organic content and word of mouth.

"The idea came from a 2025 Thailand trip, where the friends watched a street vendor press croissant dough in a waffle iron — a "croffle": flaky croissant layers with a crisp waffle texture."

The pitch

On Shark Tank, the founders asked for ₹1 crore for 1% — a ₹100 crore valuation. What they got was a different structure: ₹2.5 crore for 5% equity, implying a ₹50 crore valuation. The money was earmarked for outlet expansion in high-footfall urban locations and a digital-first, delivery-led presence. Before the show, the brand had three stores in Mumbai and had recently launched in Delhi.

The economics behind the valuation

The numbers at pitch time were modest but healthy: roughly ₹1.5 crore in first-year lifetime sales (₹40 lakh in September, with ~₹62 lakh projected for the pitch month), gross margins of about 70%, store-level EBITDA positive, and rent and salaries each under 10% of revenue. The founders' first-mover confidence play was opening outlet one directly opposite a Belgian Waffle Co. — and winning the footfall comparison.

An Indian palate

The menu is adapted to local tastes rather than copying the Thai original: ghee podi croffles, margherita croffles, and Dubai-chocolate kunafa croffles sit alongside the classics. That localization — a Thai format, Indian flavours, social-media-native branding — is the brand's real thesis: imported food ideas succeed in India when they are re-engineered for the Indian palate.

What's next

The Shark Tank round sets The Croffle Guys up for a multi-city expansion race, but it also raises the question every high-valuation food startup faces: can a single-product format scale profitably beyond its home markets? The brand's zero-marketing-cost growth so far suggests demand is real; the ₹50 crore valuation says investors are betting it travels.
